rights.summary: Alexander Alekhine died in 1946 (author copyright expired in EU/Germany on 2016-12-31 under UrhG § 64). However, this English edition was translated from the French manuscripts by J. du Mont (d. 1956) and M. E. Goldstein (d. 1966), so the English translation prose remains protected in Germany/EU until 2036-12-31 (UrhG §§ 3, 64, 65) and the McKay 1965/1972 edition bears an All Rights Reserved notice. Therefore zero verbatim book prose or OCR dumps are retained; only non-copyrightable factual chess data (PGN, SAN mainline moves, validated variation trees, diagram/key FENs, event/player/opening/result metadata) and freshly authored ChessAZ technical coaching summaries are stored.

errata.note: Summary of Results (p. vii) prints Tournaments Played=406 while Won(235)+Drawn(119)+Lost(51)=405; Index of Openings (p. 265) lists Queen's Gambit Declined twice on p. 50/185 and Ruy Lopez p. 48 twice.
Diagram after 20...c5 still prints Black's c-pawn on c6 (19...c6) while showing 20. Qxa7 already played (corrected c-pawn position is on c5).

Annotation to 23. f5 prints '23. B x P, Kt x K B P; 24. B x Kt, R x B' on p. 30; neither White bishop can capture on e3 because White's pawn occupies f4 (23. Rxe3 would fail to 23...Nxf4 24. Bxf4 Rxf4 or 23...Nxe3+).
Move 46 on p. 40 is printed as '46. Q—Kt 1'; with Black's queen on c1 blocking f1–b1, only 46. Qg1 ('Q—K Kt 1') is legal.

Printed score on p. 59 gives 46. R x P after 44...Kg5 45. Rd5+ Kf6 instead of 46. R x R (46. Rxc5 winning the rook on c5), and the note on p. 59 prints 44...R—QR5 even though a5 is occupied by Black's pawn.
Diagram on p. 75 prints the position after 30. c4 without placing Black's rook on e5 after 30...Rxe5 (e5 is shown empty even though 33...Rxe3 confirms Black's rook stands on e5).
Diagram on p. 76 draws a White knight on b3 instead of e3 (32. Na5 moved Nb3 to a5 while Ne3 remained on e3 until 33...Rxe3).
In the note to move 13, the book prints 13. PxKt (continuation numbered 12...QxB ch ... 16. Q-B 6 ch K-Q 1) starting one move number off; verified line from ply 24 is 13.cxd4 Qxc1+.

Mainline ends at 21...a4 (ply 42), where White announced mate in 10 ending '30. P-Kt 3!, any; 31. R-R 4 mate'; stored up to 30.g3 in the announced-mate variation because 'any' is not a single SAN move.
In Variation I on 11.Qd2, 11...BxB is illegal because the dark-squared bishops were already traded at move 7 (7.Nxb6 axb6); stored a cleaned note reference without the illegal branch.
Diagrams on p. 113 match the game's actual minor pieces/pawns with minor plate differences noted in early editions.

Source prints both 10. P-B 4 (f4, verified on the p. 115 diagram) and 19. P-B 4! (already on f4). Mainline is validated cleanly through 18...dxe5 (ply 36); also note move 23 prints '23. R x P ch' = 23.Rxf7+ (not Rxh7+), verified from the p. 116 diagram.

Diagram 3 on p. 118 shows 33...gxf3 (black pawn on f3, a7 pawn still present, White pawn on b6), whereas moves 35...g3, 36.Qa7, 37...b5 and Diagram 4 on p. 119 confirm 33...axb6 (printed 33...P x Kt P).
Book diagram 4 on p. 119 reflects 35...g3, 36.Qa7, 37...b5, with a minor plate difference showing f1 rook alongside c1/d1.
Move 33 prints 33...P x Kt P (33...axb6, capturing White's b6 pawn, matching 35...g3, 36.Qa7, 37...b5 and the p. 119 diagram), while the p. 118 diagram instead depicts 33...gxf3.
In the concluding text for the announced mate in two, the book misprints the final move number as '19. Kt-R 4, mate' instead of '18. Kt-R 4, mate' (17.g4! Be4 18.Nh4#).

The printed Initial Position diagram on p. 120 (and Position after 1...P-Kt 4 on p. 121) omits Black's e7 rook and White's d5 pawn, prints a6 as a5, and omits Black's b6 pawn; verified ground-truth position matches all variations and both the p. 121 (after move 4) and p. 122 (final) diagrams.
White a4 pawn already advanced/captured via 2.axb5; p. 121 diagram shows clean 6th rank PP1P1p2 without a4, matching final position.

Initial Position diagram on p. 120 and Diagram 2 on p. 121 omit Black's e7 rook, White's d5 pawn, and show White's a6 pawn on a5 and omit Black's b6 pawn. Replay of all printed variations and p. 121/p. 122 diagrams establishes startFen k1rb4/p3r3/Pp1Q1p2/3P2q1/P1P5/1R4nP/6PK/2R3B1 w - - 0 1.
Game concludes with Black's announced mate in three after 24.Qf1: '24...exd2; 25.Bd1, Ncb4!; 26.any, Nc3#'. The variation ends at ply 50 (25...Ncb4) because 'any' is not a single SAN move.

In the Alekhine-Verlinski (Odessa 1918) note after 4.Nxc3, the printed conclusion from 22.Kt x P ch through 26.R-Q 5 and the accompanying diagram omit moves/pieces relative to 14.Rd1 / 15.O-O; retained the valid 35-ply branch up to 21...Be2 and recorded the diagram FEN with printerErratum.
The diagram 'Position after White's 33rd move' places White's second rook on e1 instead of e4; text moves and the 33.Re3 / 33.Rg4 notes confirm the rook was on e4.

Score discrepancy at moves 22-25: moves 1-23.Bxe5 (with 23.B x Kt! clearly meaning 23.B x B) match the p. 154, p. 155, and p. 156 diagrams exactly, leaving Black with only light-squared Bd7. Yet the printed score next gives 23...B-Q 3! 24.BxR BxB 25.KtxB RxKt, and moves 32-33 plus the p. 157 diagram depict a black dark-squared bishop on b2. Following non-invention rules, the mainline is validated through ply 45 (23.Bxe5) and the verified checkmate finish (42.d5!..51.Rh3#) is anchored to the printed p. 157 diagram FEN.

In the London 1922 game score, move 29 prints 'R(B5)-B 6 R-K 1' (Re8) and move 31-32 reads '31.P-R 5! B-B 8  32.P-Kt 3 B-R 3  33.R-B 7 K-R 2  34.R(B6)-B 7 R-K Kt 1', which works cleanly via 33.Rf7 (from c7 to f7, clearing c7 for 34.Rcc7).

Printed diagrams on p. 180 (30th), p. 181 (36th), and p. 182 (43rd) show minor plate omissions/shifts (b4 vs a4/b3, omitted Rc6 on p. 181, omitted Ra7 on p. 182); all 120 plies of the game score replay identically in chess.js.
Printed diagram on p. 187 omits Black's g4 pawn after 32...f4.
Note at 21...Bd7 states 22.R x B ch and 23.R-R 7 ch, though after 22.Rxg7+ Kxg7 Black's king guards h7; variation retained through 22.Rxg7+.
Printed diagram after Black's 32nd move omits the Black pawn on g4 (which is present in the p. 186 move-22 diagram and moves 34...g3).
In Variation IV (13.Bd5), the book writes 14...Q-Kt 3 (Qb6), 15.Be3 Bb7, 16.Qxc5 Q-Kt 3!, repeating the square Qb6 where the Black queen already stood; variation trimmed after 16.Qxc5.
Text at 7.Q-Q 3 notes that 7...B-K 2 would allow 8.Q-Kt 4 (after 7.e5), though after 6.Qxd4 Qf6 White's e4 pawn blocks d4-g4 unless e5 is played.
Printed Final Position diagram on p. 228 places White's 8th-rank rook on h8 instead of g8 after 63.Rh1 Nd7 64.Ra1.
63. R-R 1! followed by 64. R-R 1!! with R(g8) still on g8 and R(h8)->h1->a1 explains both moves (the Final Position diagram prints the g8 rook one file right on h8).
30th-move diagram depicts White's pawn on f5 rather than Black's pawn on f4 after 28...exf4 (33rd-move diagram on p. 231 shows f4=P accurately after 33.gxf4).
In the long 33...Q-B 6! variation, the book writes 35.Q-Q 2! Q x Q, though from d5/f6 Qd4 or Qe3 is required for Q x Q.
In the final note at 22...f6, 23...Q-R 2 is blocked by Black's b7 pawn; variation stops cleanly after 23.Bh6.
Printed diagram places Black Rook on c8 instead of b8 after 28...Rb8.
Diagram places Black Rook on c8 instead of b8 (28...Rb8).
Book note labels 13...exf3 as '13...PxKt'.
Note on 34...Bxh2 writes 37.RxP! after 36...cxb6, where White continues with 37.cxb6 or Ra7.
Book note '21.BxP, BxB; 22.RxB' cannot follow 20...Bf4 directly from a dark-squared bishop.
Book note '27...QxB' after 27.Qxc4 has no bishop reachable by Qg3 (27...Bxd2 is legal).
Book note '29.Qd3 Qh2+ 30.Kf2 BxR' is blocked by White's d2 bishop.
Book note on 22...dxe5 appends '26.RxR' after 25.Rxe5 Rxe5, though White's f1 rook cannot reach e5 directly.
Book note warns against '30.KxR' after 28...Rxc1 29.Nxf6+ gxf6; King on g1 cannot capture c1.
Printed caption reads 'Position after White's 29th move' (before 29.Re1), while the diagram depicts White's rook still on f1 (after 28...Nc6).
Printed move 29...'KtxR!' is Knight takes Rook on a7 (29...Nxa7!), functioning as a queen sacrifice on e4.
Var II after 28.Qf7 prints '28...Q-R3' (Qa6), which is unreachable from d2.
Note on 42.Qxe4 claims 'mate in three moves', though 43.Kg2/43.Kxf1 avoid a forced mate in 3.

frontMatter.note: In the printed Summary of Results (p. vii), Tournaments Won (235) + Drawn (119) + Lost (51) sums to 405 while Played is printed as 406 (1922 London reports 15 played: 8 won, 7 drawn; 1923 Margate 7: 3,3,1; 1923 Carlsbad 17: 9,5,3; 1924 New York 20: 6,12,2; etc.).

variations.label: 9. Bd2 d5

variations.label: 14... hxg5 15. hxg5

variations.label: 16... h5 17. Qg3

variations.label: 18... Ke8 19. Qg1

annotations.summary: Clever defense: if White greedily takes the h1 bishop (20. Qxh1), 20...d5 21. Bb3 Qxe6 seizes the initiative.
White's 20. Qxa7! hits b7; Black advances ...c5 to contest the center before 21. d4!.
Justifies the 17. exf5 sacrifice: 21...exd4 fails immediately to 22. cxd4 cxd4 23. Ba5! forcing mate.
Black cannot stop 23. Rxb7: both 22...Qb8 23. Qa4 Rd8 and 22...Qc7 23. Rb5! lead to irresistible mating threats.

variations.label: 22... Qb8 23. Qa4
variations.summary: Forced mate after 22...Qb8.

subvariations.label: 23... Qc7 24. Rb5

annotations.summary: Wins another pawn while holding Black's bishop in a fatal pin via the threat of Ba5 and mate.
Forces ...Rxf5, after which Black drops a full piece on e7 to White's passed e6-e7 pawn and Queen checks.

Game 2: Boris Verlinsky vs Alexander Alekhine (All-Russian Amateur Tournament, 1909) — Ruy Lopez, Exchange Variation [C68], Result: 0-1.
In the Exchange Ruy Lopez endgame, Black plays 9...c4! to seize dark squares with his bishop pair, sacrifices a pawn temporarily to immobilize White's kingside, and uses central rook/knight coordination to launch a mating attack.
Line: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bb5 a6 4. Bxc6 dxc6 5. d4 exd4 6. Qxd4 Qxd4 ...

[9...c4!, p. 4] Sacrifices a pawn to fracture White's queenside pawns and seize permanent initiative with the two bishops.
[12.Nd2, p. 4] Other 12th moves also leave Black better: 12. Nd4 c5 13. Nb3 Re8 or 12. O-O Bc2 13. Nd2 Nf6 14. Ng3 Bc5 recover the pawn with superior piece play. Variations: 12. Nd4 c5 13.
